Insight


# September 2026 U.S. National Consumer Credit Trends Report


November 06, 2026


**Highlights:**


-


As of September 2026, total U.S. consumer debt reached $18.56 trillion, representing a 2.9% year-over-year increase, with mortgage debt maintaining a dominant 74.2% share of the total market.


-


Total non-mortgage debt reached $4.79 trillion, with auto loans and leases accounting for 36.5% and student loans making up 26.9% of the non-mortgage portfolio.


As of September 2026, the monthly Equifax Consumer Credit Trends Report showed that total U.S. consumer debt was $18.56 trillion, up 2.9% from September 2025. Mortgage debt, including home equity loans, accounted for $13.77 trillion, a 74.2% share of total consumer debt, while non-mortgage consumer debt totaled $4.79 trillion, with 36.5% of non-mortgage consumer debt attributable to auto loans and leases, and 26.9% attributable to student loans.


Outstanding balances on auto loans and leases increased 3.7% from September 2025, to $1.74 trillion in September 2026.


Outstanding balances on U.S. bankcards increased versus the prior month to $1.13 trillion in September 2026, up 3.9% from September 2025. Average bankcard utilization stood at 20.3%, which is a slight decrease from 20.8% in September 2025.


#### Consumer Credit Observations:


-


As of September 2026, total U.S. consumer debt was $18.56 trillion, up 2.9% from September 2025.


-


Mortgage debt, including home equity loans, accounted for $13.77 trillion, making up 74.2% of total U.S. consumer debt.


-


First mortgages were 94.8% of mortgage debt outstanding.


-


Home Equity Lines of Credit (HELOCs) were 3.4% of mortgage debt outstanding.


-


Non-mortgage debt totaled $4.79 trillion in September 2026 and broke down into:


-


-


36.5% from auto loans and leases.


-


26.9% from student loans.


-


24.6% from credit card balances.


-


12% from other products.

Download the[August 2026 National Consumer Credit Trends Report](https://assets.equifax.com/marketing/US/assets/portfolio-credit-trends-sept26.pdf) now for the latest full dataset.


**Auto Loans and Leases Observations:**


-


Total outstanding balances on auto loans and leases increased 3.7% from September 2025 to $1.74 trillion.


-


The number of outstanding accounts in September 2026 was 87.2 million, a 0.2% increase year-over-year.


-


The severe balance delinquency (60+ days past due) rate in September 2026 was 1.5%, which is 7 basis points down from September of last year.


**Bankcard Portfolio Observations:**


-


Outstanding balances on bankcards increased 3.9% from September 2025 to $1.13 trillion.


-


The number of outstanding accounts was 604.6 million in September 2026, a 3.1% increase from September 2025.


-


The severe balance delinquency rate (60+ days past due) as of September 2026 was 2.74%, which is a 9 basis point decrease from September 2025 (2.83%).


-


Average bankcard utilization for September 2026 was 20.3%, compared to 20.8% in September of 2025.


Equifax publishes monthly U.S. Consumer Credit Insights[here](https://www.equifax.com/business/trends-insights/marketpulse/) — including information on private-label credit cards, consumer finance, student loans, and credit originations. Additionally, global consumer credit trends from the first half of 2026 can be explored in the report[here](https://assets.equifax.com/marketing/US/assets/global-credit-trends-1h-26-report.pdf) .
